name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation College Scholarship
description: U.S. high school seniors graduating spring 2027 and entering an accredited four-year college in fall 2027; minimum unweighted GPA 3.75, required SAT/ACT/AP/IB test score, and financial need with family income reviewed up to $95,000.

name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
description: For Black/African American high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and demonstrate academic achievement, leadership, service and financial need. Awards total $40,000 over four years; essays and recommendations are required.

name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
description: Need-based awards of up to $25,000 for high school juniors who have overcome adversity and demonstrate leadership, service and academic commitment. Check the sponsor for the next application cycle and detailed eligibility; high school seniors should review its other programs.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for the next junior-year application cycle

name: Scholarships360 $10,000 No-Essay Scholarship
description: Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents across high school, undergraduate, graduate, technical and vocational programs. Rolling monthly entry deadlines; one $10,000 award for the cycle, with finalist interviews.

name: U.S. Bank Student Scholarship Program
description: Legal U.S. residents age 17+, accepted or enrolled in an eligible undergraduate college or trade/vocational program. Financial education modules required; a sweepstakes rather than a need-based award.

name: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars Program
description: Thirteen $25,000 awards recognize students for academic success, community service and financial need. Includes a one-year leadership development and mentoring program; review the sponsor application for full eligibility.

name: Mensa Foundation U.S. Scholarship
description: Enrolled in a degree program at an accredited U.S. institution. Requires an essay of up to 550 words on career goals.

name: VFW Voice of Democracy Scholarship Contest
description: For eligible students in grades 9–12. Submit an original audio essay on the current patriotic theme with an entry form through a participating local VFW Post. National, state and local awards vary.
deadlineLabel: October 31, 2026, midnight; submit through your participating VFW Post

name: Space to Succeed Scholarship
description: For legal U.S. residents age 18+ attending an accredited U.S. college or university. Submit a 500–800 word essay about community involvement, plus required photos and enrollment documentation; three awards in this cycle.

name: Financial Goals Scholarship
description: U.S. residents age 18 or older who are planning to enroll or currently enrolled in a college degree program; written response required.

name: Union Plus Scholarship
description: For eligible current or retired participating-union members, spouses and dependent children. Applicants must meet membership and enrollment rules; essays weigh heavily in selection. Awards are one-time, but students may reapply in later years.

name: Truman Scholars Program
description: A graduate-study scholarship for eligible college students committed to public-service careers. Applicants must be nominated by their institution; check campus nomination deadlines before the national deadline.
deadlineLabel: February 2, 2027, 11:59 p.m. in your time zone; campus deadlines may be earlier

name: The Christophers Video Contest
description: College student video contest; original video no longer than five minutes interpreting One Person Can Make a Difference. Sponsor prohibits AI-generated video.

name: Stossel in the Classroom Video Contest
description: Middle school grades5–8, high school grades9–12, or undergraduate college students residing in the U.S./Canada or with a U.S. military address. Submit a one-to-three-minute video on a current prompt.

name: Debt.com Scholarship for Aggressive Applicants
categoryLabel: No essay required to apply broadly
description: Apply to as many scholarships as possible (winning isn't required) and submit proof plus a short statement about the experience.

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
description: Achievement-based awards recognizing leadership and service among eligible students in their final year of high school. The program selects 150 students for $20,000 awards; current citizenship/residency, GPA and school requirements apply.
deadlineLabel: 2027 application is closed; check sponsor for next cycle

name: The Gates Scholarship
description: A highly selective, last-dollar scholarship for outstanding high school seniors from low-income households. Check the official application for current eligibility, funding coverage, required materials and deadlines.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current application rules and dates

name: Dell Scholars Program
description: For the 2027 cycle: Texas high school seniors planning to attend an accredited four-year PUBLIC college or university in Texas; participation in an approved college-readiness program in grades11–12, Pell eligibility and GPA2.4+ required.

name: QuestBridge National College Match
description: Connects high-achieving high school seniors from low-income backgrounds with partner colleges and full four-year Match Scholarships. Review citizenship, academic and financial criteria and the binding Match process before ranking colleges.
deadlineLabel: 2026 Match applicants have been selected as Finalists; check sponsor for next entry cycle

name: Burger King Scholars Program
description: Scholarships for eligible high school seniors, Burger King employees and employee families pursuing postsecondary college or vocational/technical education. Awards and criteria vary by application track; check the administrator for current requirements.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current application cycle

name: Elks MVS Scholarship
description: Current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens and plan full-time four-year undergraduate study at an accredited U.S. college. Elks membership/relationship not required.

name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
description: LGBTQ+ AND ally students, at least high school seniors, with GPA3.3+ pursuing full-time undergraduate/graduate/professional degrees at accredited U.S. not-for-profit institutions. 100%online degree programs excluded.
deadlineLabel: November 19, 5 p.m. Pacific (fall 2027 funding; confirm cycle)

name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund Scholar Program
description: Merit-selected HSF Scholars receive support services and may receive a cash award based on need and available funding. Hispanic-heritage students must meet citizenship/residency, GPA and full-time enrollment requirements; a Scholar designation does not guarantee a cash award.
deadlineLabel: 2026 application closed; check sponsor for the next cycle

name: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
description: Scholarships for American Indian and Alaska Native students in certificate, undergraduate or graduate programs at tribal colleges and universities or accredited nonprofit schools. One annual application covers multiple opportunities; eligibility and funding vary.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current application and priority dates

name: UNCF Scholarships
description: UNCF administers a range of scholarships, fellowships and other student opportunities. Each program has its own school, major, eligibility, essay and deadline requirements; use the official opportunities portal to find a match.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
description: For students 18 and under who have completed a significant piece of work in science, technology, math, literature, music, philosophy or outside the box categories.
deadlineLabel: 2027 applications open November 2, 2026; check sponsor for deadline

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
description: Entry begins through qualifying PSAT/NMSQT participation and program requirements. Semifinalists must complete an application including an essay and meet additional requirements to become Finalists; this is not a no-essay scholarship.

name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
description: Graduating high school seniors who are U.S. citizens, demonstrate financial need, academic excellence, leadership and community service, and plan an approved four-year college. Transcript, test score, CSS Profile, essays and recommendation required.

name: Hagan Scholarship
description: A renewable scholarship with funding determined by educational costs and other aid, plus required workshops and student responsibilities. Review the sponsor’s current academic, income, enrollment and work requirements before applying.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current application cycle

name: Children of Fallen Patriots Foundation Scholarship
description: College and trade-school scholarships, educational assistance and career support for military children who lost a parent in the line of duty. The program is joining Tunnel to Towers and states that scholarship processing continues; contact the sponsor to confirm eligibility and funding.
deadlineLabel: Contact sponsor about enrollment and funding

name: Imagine America Career College Scholarships
description: Tuition discounts/grants at participating career colleges through separate high-school, adult-learner and military programs. Check your chosen school and program requirements; this is tuition assistance at partner schools rather than unrestricted cash.

name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
amount: Up to $18,000 associate / $36,000 bachelor, plus possible stipends
description: For eligible low-income Dreamer students attending a participating in-state or online Partner College. Current rules include U.S. arrival before age 16 and before November 1, 2021; international students and temporary nonimmigrant statuses are ineligible. Review all immigration, residency, GPA and enrollment criteria directly with the sponsor.
deadlineLabel: Check sponsor for current National Scholarship cycle

name: AAUW Career Development Grant
description: Women with at least an associate degree pursuing a short-term accredited certificate/training program in a field where women are underrepresented. Not for a bachelor/master/professional degree program.

name: Jeannette Rankin National Scholar Grant
description: Unrestricted, nontuition grants for eligible students age 35+ who self-identify and present as women, pursuing technical/vocational education, a first associate degree or first bachelor degree at an accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. Review income and other sponsor criteria.

name: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Award
description: Women with financial need providing primary financial support for themselves AND dependents, enrolled or accepted into undergraduate or vocational training; additional country and prior-award restrictions apply.

name: Taco Bell Foundation Live Más Scholarship
description: For eligible new applicants ages 16–26 pursuing postsecondary education. Submit either a 30-second–2-minute video or a 250–500-word essay about passion, community and impact. No GPA or test-score requirement; financial need is considered for new 2027 applicants.

name: American Legion Legacy Scholarship
amount: Up to $20,000 for children of fallen / $5,000 for children of disabled veterans
description: Need-based support for eligible children of U.S. servicemembers who died on active duty on or after September 11, 2001, or post-9/11 veterans with a VA combined disability rating of at least 50%. Review documentation and other aid requirements directly with the sponsor.
deadlineLabel: Last posted 2026 application closed; check sponsor for next cycle

name: DAR Pittenger American History Scholarship
description: For a graduating high school senior pursuing an undergraduate degree with at least 24 credit hours in American history or American government. The$2,000 award may be renewed for up to four years under GPA and transcript requirements; see sponsor for details.
deadlineLabel: Check DAR scholarship portal for current cycle

name: National Honor Society Scholarship
description: Active National Honor Society members who are high school seniors demonstrating leadership, service and scholarship, planning to attend college.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year Scholarships
description: Scholarships for participants advancing through Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year recognition. State winners receive $2,500, regional winners $20,000 and the National Youth of the Year $50,000. Ask your Club about participation and its selection process.
deadlineLabel: Contact your Club about its selection timeline

name: Sallie$2,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: For legal residents of the 50 U.S. states, D.C. or U.S. territories age 16+ who meet the specified college-student, high-school-junior/senior or parent eligibility. Monthly sweepstakes; no essay required. Review official rules before entering.
deadlineLabel: Monthly entry periods; see sponsor for current deadline

name: Niche $2,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: A no-essay drawing for eligible high school, college and graduate students or those planning enrollment within 12 months. Entrants age 13–17 require parental consent/supervision; citizenship or valid-visa and other official-rule restrictions apply.
deadlineLabel: Monthly sweepstakes periods; confirm current rules

name: Unigo $10,000 Scholarship
description: U.S. legal residents age 14 or older; short original written response of 250 words or fewer required.

name: Appily Easy Money Scholarship
description: A monthly no-essay scholarship for eligible U.S. students age 13+ who create a free Appily account and plan postsecondary enrollment. Complete the profile and entry requirements in the official rules; one winner is selected each month.

name: DoSomething.org Easy Scholarships
description: For people ages 13–25 living in the U.S. or U.S. citizens abroad who complete an eligible community-service action and report back. No essay, GPA or recommendation requirement; each action has its own location, rules, award and deadline.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
description: Art and writing recognition and scholarship opportunities for eligible teen entrants. Portfolio scholarships for high school seniors submitting six works can reach$12,500; other awards and regional rules differ. Review current grade, age and submission requirements.

name: YoungArts
description: A national visual, literary and performing arts competition for eligible students in grades 10–12 or ages 15–18, with U.S. citizenship, residency or taxable-income eligibility requirements. Winners receive cash awards and career/mentorship support.
deadlineLabel: Current application closed; next 2028 application opens summer 2027

name: Society of Women Engineers (SWE) Scholarship Program
description: Scholarships for students in eligible engineering, technology and related programs. Undergraduate tracks require an eligible ABET-accredited program; year-of-study, GPA, graduate-major and regional requirements differ. Recommendations are required; check the relevant application.

name: AICPA Foundation Legacy Scholarships
description: Awards supporting eligible accounting students pursuing CPA careers, with separate Future CPAs, first-generation/public accounting and two-year-transfer opportunities. GPA, citizenship/residency, enrollment and other rules differ; one application can cover eligible Legacy awards.
deadlineLabel: Check the relevant Legacy scholarship for current dates

name: National FFA Scholarships
description: One application covers multiple scholarship opportunities for senior FFA members in high school and FFA alumni in college, pursuing trade certificates, two-year or four-year programs. Individual sponsors set additional eligibility criteria.
